summary.one_liner: LiveCode Community Edition is an open source development environment for building cross-platform mobile, desktop and server applications with a visual, "live" workflow and its own English-like language syntax.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains the source for the LiveCode Community engine, which loads, saves, manages and runs LiveCode stack files. It is organized into subprojects: the main engine (engine/), static support libraries (libcore, libexternal, libexternalv1), and dynamically loaded externals for database access (revdb), iOS and Android support (revmobile), PDF printing (revpdfprinter), text-to-speech (revspeech), video capture on Windows (revvideograbber), XML (revxml), and zip archives (revzip). The engine is built in four flavours: IDE, installer, server (no GUI, CGI support), and standalone (embedded in apps made with LiveCode). The build uses the gyp tool to generate Xcode, Visual Studio, or Linux makefile project files. The README includes a table of target platforms versus host platforms for building, such as iOS and macOS builds requiring a Mac host, and Windows builds possible from Wine on Linux.
use_cases: Build cross-platform desktop applications with a visual IDE
Develop mobile apps for iOS and Android
Create server-side applications with CGI support
Compile the LiveCode engine from source
Contribute patches to an open source development environment
Generate platform-specific project files with gyp
how_to_run: Clone the LiveCode git repository from GitHub
On Linux or Mac, install basic development tools
notable: Four engine flavours (IDE, installer, server, standalone) exposed as separate build targets
Uses gyp to generate Xcode, Visual Studio, and makefile projects
Modular externals loaded at runtime, such as database, PDF, speech, and XML
Run by LiveCode Ltd. since the Community edition launched in April 2013
caveats: Building iOS and macOS targets requires a Mac host; Windows builds on Linux go through Wine
Only compilable from a git clone of the repository, not from a source archive
Pre-compiled binaries are provided separately via the LiveCode download centre
